accepted.title: Generalized Tarski problem with the finite radical
accepted.text: A group is acylindrically hyperbolic if it admits a non-elementary acylindrical isometric action on a Gromov-hyperbolic space; acylindrical means that for each ε>0 there are R,N such that at most N elements move each of any two points distance≥R by≤ε. For every such G, write E(G) for its maximal finite normal subgroup and G*=⟨G,t | [t,e]=1 for all e∈E(G)⟩=G*ₑ₍G₎(E(G)×ℤ). Are G and G* elementarily equivalent? More strongly, is the canonical inclusion G→G* an elementary embedding?

accepted.title: Virtual cohomology spectra of limit groups and HGFC-groups
accepted.text: A limit group is a finitely generated fully residually free group: every finite subset is mapped injectively by some homomorphism to a free group. An HGFC-group is a word-hyperbolic group which is the fundamental group of a finite graph of finitely generated free groups with infinite cyclic edge groups. For a given such G, field k and integer i≥0, determine Spectrumᵏᵢ(G)={dimₖ Hⁱ(H;k):H≤G and [G:H]<∞}. In particular, which integers occur, rather than merely whether this set is bounded?
accepted.subject: Group Theory & Geometric Group Theory

accepted.title: Rigidity from filtered second Betti spectra
accepted.text: A limit group is a finitely generated fully residually free group: every finite subset is mapped injectively by some homomorphism to a free group. An HGFC-group is a word-hyperbolic group which is the fundamental group of a finite graph of finitely generated free groups with infinite cyclic edge groups. For each field k let FSpectrum²ₖ(G)={dimₖ H²(H;k)/[G:H]:H≤G and [G:H]<∞}. Which groups G in the union of the limit-group and HGFC classes are characterized up to isomorphism within that union by this invariant? That is, for which G does equality FSpectrum²ₖ(G)=FSpectrum²ₖ(H) force H≅G for every H in these classes?
